answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line at 94% committed volume with no buffer, switching vendors now carries high delivery-risk exposure that outweighs potential cost savings, especially since memory_c2's favorable switch outcome was under different market conditions a year ago and unverified for current lead times. The incumbent has already refused to reopen price this cycle, so an immediate negotiate_terms push is unlikely to succeed before expiry. Verifying memory_c1 (stability of incumbent renewal) and memory_c6 (multi-year volume pricing) lets me confirm whether a short-term renewal with a longer-term pricing lever is still viable. I intend to renew the incumbent now to protect delivery continuity, while flagging that the 18% cost mandate remains unmet and must be addressed next cycle via renegotiation or a qualified second source, per memory_c3's precedent on reducing single-point risk without disrupting current supply.
